title: Microsoft 365 admin center: cross-tenant orchestrated migration of user and shared data
summary: Hold: the prerequisites put the MailUser in the wrong tenant, and the checklist schedules identity mapping before its security-group prerequisite. Microsoft also publishes Shared Data Migration licensing for the existing SharePoint migration feature, and the Complete After Date is an earliest cutover time, not a guaranteed cutover time.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans cross-tenant orchestrated migration in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center: Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration

claims.claim: The roadmap's UDM scope moves user mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, Teams chats and Teams meetings between tenants.
claims.quote: UDM includes the ability to move user mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, Teams chats, and Teams meetings.

claims.claim: The roadmap's SDM scope includes Microsoft 365 Groups, SharePoint sites, group mailboxes, and teams and channels.
claims.quote: SDM includes the ability to move M365 Groups, SharePoint Sites, Group Mailboxes, and teams and channels.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The listed release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn's user-data orchestrator supports selecting Exchange mailboxes, OneDrives, Teams chats and Teams meetings when creating a batch.
claims.quote: There are four supported workloads that can be specified to be moved when creating a batch: Exchange mailboxes, OneDrives, Teams chats, and Teams meetings.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The documented Cross-Tenant User Data Migration solution excludes shared data such as Teams and channels and SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: The Cross-Tenant User Data Migration solution doesn't migrate shared data, such as Teams and Channels or SharePoint Sites. This data remains in the source tenant.

claims.claim: The documented orchestrator is managed through Microsoft Graph APIs, including PowerShell.
claims.quote: Migrations are managed through Graph APIs. These APIs can be run with PowerShell 5 or 7, or with Graph Explorer.

claims.claim: No Microsoft 365 admin center path for starting an orchestrated migration batch is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant orchestrated migration admin center start cancel batch default enabled shared data migration orchestration; "migration orchestrator" "admin center" "start" "cancel". Opened Running the migration and Moving from multitenant to migration readiness; no batch-start UI found.

claims.claim: No Microsoft 365 admin center path for cancelling an orchestrated migration batch is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "migration orchestrator" "admin center" "start" "cancel"; cross tenant orchestrated migration admin center start cancel batch default enabled shared data migration orchestration. Opened Running the migration; cancellation is documented through Graph PowerShell, not an admin-center path.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document the roadmap's SDM orchestration, its controls, detailed scoping, limits or prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: "cross-tenant" "orchestrated" "SDM"; "orchestrated" "shared data" migration SDM controls scope prerequisites. Opened orchestrator Overview, Planning and prerequisites, and Cross-tenant SharePoint migration; no roadmap SDM orchestration documentation found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The arrival default of the planned admin-center experience is not stated, and no source says existing tenants automatically change.
claims.quote: Searched: "cross-tenant" "orchestrator" "admin center" "default"; cross tenant orchestrated migration admin center start cancel batch default enabled shared data migration orchestration. Read roadmap, Overview and Running the migration; none states the planned admin-center arrival default.

claims.claim: The documented UDM migration moves content, not identities.
claims.quote: This migration moves content, not identities.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Customers must create and configure the target users.
claims.quote: Customers are responsible for correctly creating and configuring users, and the product moves the in-scope content from its source tenant location to its target tenant location.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Identity mapping is required for every migrating user before migration.
claims.quote: We require all users migrating content must be mapped in the identity mapping system before any migration takes place.

claims.claim: Cross-Tenant Identity Mapping maps source users one-to-one to target users.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant Identity Mapping (CTIM) is a tool that allows source users to be mapped one-to-one to target users.

claims.claim: Users are grouped into batches of at most 100.
claims.quote: Users are grouped together into a batch and submitted together. The maximum batch size is 100 users.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The batch must pass validation before migration starts.
claims.quote: The job must pass validation before migration can start.

claims.claim: Exchange mailbox synchronization runs in the background before the Complete After Date.
claims.quote: Before this time, only syncing (and specifically, Exchange syncing) will happen in the background.

claims.where: What's changing, third paragraph; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Mailboxes cut over at the Complete After Date and then OneDrive, Teams chats and Teams meetings begin moving.
claims.quote: completeAfterDateTime - The date that specifies the earliest acceptable time for the cutover of Exchange to begin. There's no user impact until this date passes and the Exchange sync is complete.
claims.fix: Replace the timing statement with: 'The Complete After Date is the earliest acceptable time for Exchange cutover to begin; it also requires Exchange synchronization to be complete. If Exchange is selected, it cuts over before the other selected workloads begin moving.' Apply this qualification to What's changing, Autonomy & actions and the impact rationale. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/enterprise/migration-orchestrator-5-running-migration.

claims.claim: The source mailbox is deleted after successful migration.
claims.quote: The source mailbox is deleted after a successful migration.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A batch can only be cancelled before the Complete After Date passes.
claims.quote: A batch can only be canceled before the Complete After Date is reached. After this point, the migration continues without cancelation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented orchestrator requires preparation, applications and permissions in both tenants.
claims.quote: To enable migration, add the applications for Cross-Tenant Migration Service, OneDrive Migration, Teams Chat Migration, and Teams Meeting Migration, add permissions to those applications, and run additional setup steps.

claims.claim: The documented migration requires an administrator-created batch rather than automatically moving tenant data.
claims.quote: The migration is run by creating a migration job in the form of a batch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: At least one source-tenant mail-enabled security group is required to scope whose content can move.
claims.quote: At least one mail-enabled security group is required in the source tenant. These groups are used to: Scope the list of users whose content can move from source tenant to the target tenant.

claims.claim: The source group's scoping prevents unintended users being migrated or their data accessed.
claims.quote: This scoping allows the source tenant administrator to restrict access to a specific set of users whose content needs to be moved, preventing unintended users from being migrated or their data accessed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Mailboxes on any type of hold are blocked from migration.
claims.quote: Mailboxes on any type of hold aren't migrated, and a move for those mailboxes is blocked.

claims.claim: After migration the source mailbox is not available, discoverable or accessible in the source tenant.
claims.quote: This deletion means that, after migration, under no circumstances is the source mailbox available, discoverable, or accessible in the source tenant.

claims.claim: Original Teams content remains in the source tenant, possibly edited.
claims.quote: The original content on the source remains, though it might be in an edited form.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Change & support
claims.claim: Duplicate Teams threads might exist in both tenants.
claims.quote: There might be duplicate threads created on both tenants.

claims.claim: Tenant configuration adds many permissions to tenant applications, including the migration service and Teams chat and meeting migration apps.
claims.quote: When you run the tenant configuration steps, there are many permissions added to your tenant and applications.

claims.claim: Teams chat migration requires federated users to be allowed in both tenants.
claims.quote: These instructions must be run from both the source and the target tenant. ... Federated users must be allowed. Run the cmdlet: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $True

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Migration commands run from the target tenant as Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator or Global Administrator, not from the source tenant.
claims.quote: All commands below are run through Microsoft Graph from the target tenant by Microsoft M365 Migration Administrators or Global Administrators. Source tenants cannot run the migration commands.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends using the role with the fewest permissions instead of Global Administrator where possible.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends that you use roles with the fewest permissions. ... Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that should be limited to emergency scenarios when you can't use an existing role.

claims.claim: OneDrive cutover removes the source OneDrive and gives the target user a OneDrive.
claims.quote: OneDrive, if selected, begins to cutover from source to target, giving the target user a OneDrive and removing the source OneDrive.

claims.claim: Migrations are not subject to SLAs.
claims.quote: Migrations are not subject to SLAs.

claims.claim: Migration size and overall traffic determine completion time.
claims.quote: The size of your migration including the number of users and their associated content, as well as overall traffic, will determine the completion time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Target users must not have mailboxes or OneDrive sites provisioned before migration because that makes migration fail.
claims.quote: Users must not have mailboxes or OneDrive sites provisioned on the target before migration. This provisioning would make the migration fail.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: After migration users should use only their target identity for Teams.
claims.quote: Once the migration completes, users should only use their target identity to use Teams.

claims.claim: After the move the source user mailbox is converted to a MailUser.
claims.quote: After the moves are complete, the source user mailbox is converted to a MailUser, and the targetAddress (shown as ExternalEmailAddress in Exchange) is stamped with the routing address to the destination tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented Cross Tenant User Data Migration licence is an add-on.
claims.quote: Cross Tenant User Data Migration is available as an add-on to the following Microsoft 365 subscription plans:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The UDM migration licence is required per user and carries a one-time fee.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee)

claims.claim: The migration licence can be assigned to either the source or the target user object.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee) and can be assigned on either the source or target user object.

claims.claim: The UDM licence enables migration of all content supported by the documented orchestrator.
claims.quote: This license enables the migration of all content supported by orchestration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The add-on plan list includes Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard, Premium, F1, F3, E3, E5; Office 365 F3, E1, E3, E5; Exchange Online; SharePoint in Microsoft 365; OneDrive; and EDU.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard, and Premium; Microsoft 365 F1/F3/E3/E5; Office 365 F3/E1/E3/E5; Exchange Online; SharePoint in Microsoft 365; OneDrive; EDU

claims.claim: The overview says UDM is available to EA, CSP, Web direct, small business and EDU customers.
claims.quote: This product is available for EA, CSP, Web direct, small business, and EDU customers.
claims.fix: Keep the overview's statement and append: 'The separate OneDrive migration licensing page still describes the add-on for Enterprise Agreement customers as of November 2022; confirm purchase eligibility with Microsoft.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration?view=o365-worldwide#licensing, whose wording is 'for Enterprise Agreement customers'.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The overview publishes no fee amount for the per-user UDM add-on.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cross Tenant User Data Migration" license price fee; "Cross Tenant User Data Migration" "price" "$". Read Overview licensing and availability, plus mailbox and OneDrive licensing search excerpts; no UDM fee amount stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has published no licence for Shared Data Migration.
claims.quote: The Cross-Tenant Shared Data Migration feature and licenses are currently only available to Enterprise Agreement customers. ... Licenses are offered on a per 100 GB of data moved basis.
claims.fix: Replace the broad licensing absence everywhere, including the notes and cost rationale, with: 'For the separate cross-tenant SharePoint migration feature, Microsoft publishes Cross-Tenant Shared Data Migration licences for Enterprise Agreement customers, per 100 GB of data moved. Licensing specific to the roadmap's SDM orchestration is not yet published.' Narrow the open question to licensing for the roadmap's SDM orchestration. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration?view=o365-worldwide.

claims.claim: Licensing specific to the planned admin-center experience is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Cross Tenant Shared Data Migration licensing price orchestrator SDM; cross tenant orchestrated migration admin center start cancel batch default enabled shared data migration orchestration. Read roadmap, Overview and Cross-tenant SharePoint migration; no admin-center-specific entitlement found.

claims.claim: The prerequisites require users to have a Teams licence in both tenants.
claims.quote: All users need a Teams license on both tenants. Assign the user a license on both tenants.

claims.claim: The prerequisites require users to have an Exchange Online licence in both tenants.
claims.quote: All users must have an Exchange Online license in both tenants

claims.claim: Source and target administrators need Global Administrator access on their respective tenants for tenant and user configuration.
claims.quote: Global administrator access for source and target admins on their respective tenant, which is required to manage the tenant and user configuration steps.

claims.claim: All users submitted in the batch must belong to the provided scope security group.
claims.quote: All users submitted in the batch must belong to the provided scope security group

claims.claim: A source MailUser configuration for each migrating user is a migration prerequisite.
claims.quote: The product does, however, require that a user be specifically configured as having a mailbox on the source tenant and not having a mailbox on the target tenant (MailUser) before Identity Mapping can be performed.
claims.fix: Replace 'a source MailUser configuration for each migrating user' with 'a target MailUser configuration for each migrating user'. The source retains its mailbox before migration; the MailUser prerequisite is in the target tenant. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/migration-orchestrator-1-overview?view=o365-worldwide.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, workload bullet
claims.claim: Learn recommends migrating multiple selected workloads together in the same batch.
claims.quote: If you intend to run the migration of multiple workloads (such as Exchange, chats, meetings, and OneDrive), you should run them all together in the same batch, rather than managing separate batches for individual workloads.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, workload bullet
claims.claim: A batch selecting Teams meetings without Teams chats and mailboxes fails to initiate.
claims.quote: The migration batch will fail to initiate if the Teams meeting workload is selected without also selecting Teams chats and mailboxes.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Migration-scope group membership changes can take up to an hour to be processed.
claims.quote: There's up to an hour-long delay between when updates are made to the group containing the authorized users for migration and when our system processes those changes.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, validation bullet
claims.claim: Validation must reach ValidatePassed and remain no more than seven days old when migration starts.
claims.quote: Validation must pass within the last seven days. If more than seven days elapsed since validation passed, you must revalidate before migrating.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, last bullet
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends submitting batches two weeks before the Complete After Date for background synchronization without user impact.
claims.quote: We strongly recommend submitting batches two weeks before the CompleteAfterDate as there's no impact on the end users during synchronization.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Calling migrate again on a CompletedWithErrors or Failed batch retries unsuccessful migrations.
claims.quote: If a migration completes with errors (Status: CompletedWithErrors) or fails (Status: Failed), you can call migrate again on the same batch to retry.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/solutions/migrations/crossTenantMigrationJobs/{crossTenantMigrationJobId}/migrate starts the migration of a validated job.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/solutions/migrations/crossTenantMigrationJobs/add14989-2b21-4001-81bd-a18b0bac1dea/migrate

claims.claim: Stop-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id> cancels a batch.
claims.quote: Stop-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id>

claims.claim: Cancellation covers users whose mailboxes have not cut over and whose Teams and OneDrive migrations have not started.
claims.quote: It cancels all migrations for users whose mailboxes aren't yet cut over and whose Teams Chats, Teams Meetings, and OneDrive migrations aren't started.

claims.claim: The separate cross-tenant SharePoint migration feature lets SharePoint admins move sites using SharePoint Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: SharePoint sites can now be moved from one tenant to another using the Cross-tenant SharePoint migration feature. SharePoint Admins can transition sites into their new tenants using SharePoint Online PowerShell.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, last bullet; At rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The checklist can run identity mapping before creating and populating the source migration-scope security group.
claims.quote: If the source users aren't already added into the mail-enabled security group you created before, this addition must be done before Identity Mapping is complete.
claims.fix: Move the existing 'Create the mail-enabled security group in the source tenant and add the users whose content may move; allow up to an hour for membership changes to be processed' bullet into Before rollout, immediately before the target-user creation and identity-mapping bullet. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/migration-orchestrator-4-user-prep?view=o365-worldwide for this ordering.

claims.claim: The checklist names controls that are not represented in the two-row controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Decide which workloads move'; 'run Cross-Tenant Identity Mapping'; 'keep mailboxes and OneDrive sites from being provisioned'; 'Create the mail-enabled security group'; 'Create and validate the batch'; 'Monitor batch and per-user status'. Table: starting and cancelling only.
claims.fix: The checklist steps for workload selection, identity mapping, target-provisioning prevention, scope-group membership, batch creation/validation, status monitoring and source-MailUser cleanup have no corresponding controls-table rows. This finding identifies the mismatch only; it does not request additional rows.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, last bullet
claims.claim: The source tenant can remove the source MailUser or convert it when business processes allow.
claims.quote: When business processes allow, the source tenant can remove the source MailUser or convert them to a mail contact.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The documented orchestrator exposes batch-level and per-user migration status for monitoring.
claims.quote: Monitor the status at the batch level (Retrieve a specific batch) and at the user level (Retrieve user status within a specific batch).

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Migrated users use their target tenant account for the migrated mailbox.
claims.quote: Users can use their target tenant accounts to use their mailboxes, chats, meetings, and OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: The documented migration setup uses the Microsoft Graph PowerShell beta module.
claims.quote: The following modules are prerequisites to importing the CrossTenantMigration module. ... Microsoft.Graph.Beta (minimum version 2.33.0)
